$comment: Executable ISA table: the source of truth for asm/ and disasm/.
Hand-derived from docs/DSP_ISA_SPEC.md; that file stays
the documentation and tests/test_spec.py cross-checks the two.
when    literals a decoded word must match (absent field = don't care).
A name like 'b76' is a synthetic field defined in word.synthetic.
fields  field <- source. Source is an integer literal, an operand name,
or {'from': operand, 'bits': [..]} to extract bit positions.
result  the semantics, straight from the spec.
An operand marked 'immediate': true takes the instruction's immediate
value; spec 4.4 allows exactly one such value per instruction, so the
immediate operands of a variant share it.
status tags follow the spec: exact | measured | inferred | fitted |
unknown. Only exact/measured/inferred/fitted variants get a mnemonic.
Everything else is preserved verbatim by the 'raw' form, and reported.

alu.$doc: spec 5.1: units A and B share this layout

X.$doc: unit B: the nibble at 11-8 is op*2 + X[2], so X[2] lives in the nibble

synthetic.$doc: Fields the spec names that are not their own contiguous field of the ALU word: b11_8 (the nibble: op*2 + X[2] for unit B) and f_family (nibble F only: 00 special functions, 01 f4..f7). Bits 5-4 are always the `mode` field of the ALU layout; the nibble-E/F families reuse them as a function/sub-op selector.

b11_8.$doc: the nibble: op*2 + X[2] for a unit-B op

f_family.$doc: nibble F only: 00 = special functions, 01 = f4/f5/f6/f7 (spec 6.4)

Y.$doc: bits 2-0 = register; bit 3 is not a negation (measured 2026-10-20, DISCREPANCIES D3): for a register it is a free bit, restored with .free. Immediate modes use bits 3-0 as the byte.

W.$doc: bit 3 negates a register W (measured 2026-10-20: mac_p1 with -r3 gives X*Y - r3)

mac.$doc_op2: spec 5.2: bits 11-10 are the coefficient mode (0 = rC, 2 = imm24, 3 = imm32), and bit 9 is 1 when the coefficient is a register. In the corpus bit 9 is set for every op2 = 0 word that uses C (0x9281 = Z=-r1, C=r2: 0b100 1 010 00 0001), so coefreg=1 is the register-coefficient form.

field_relations.$doc:
How fields of a form relate, declared rather than inferred.
  same_bits_as   two fields name the same bits; naming either covers both
  selector_only  the field is a selector: only variants that test it own it,
                 and for the others the same bits belong to `of`
  optional       a field some variants carry and others simply do not use

field_sources.$doc: How a variant's `fields` map names its sources: an integer is a literal; an operand name puts the whole operand in the field; {"from": name, "range": [msb, lsb]} takes that bit range of the operand value (inclusive, shifted down), after adding `add` and then OR-ing `or`.

immediate.alu_read: byte Y of the slot array (Y = the op's 4-bit field)
immediate.mac_read: Y at byte Y, W at byte W; the coefficient c right after Y's immediate

width_policy.$doc: Which immediate width an operand takes (spec 4.4). The width is a property of the variant, not a global 'narrowest': spec 11.2 uses imm32 for `mul` while 11.3 uses imm16 for `mov`. Variants that do not say use the narrowest width that holds the value exactly.

byte_offsets.$doc: spec 4.4: an op with immediate mode reads it starting at byte Y of the slot array, so Y is a *byte offset* into the stream, not a value. When one instruction carries several immediates their offsets must be written explicitly; the disassembler prints them as sel=BYTE.

number_format.$doc: spec 2: sign-magnitude, exponent steps of x16
number_format.rule: smallest exponent with mantissa < 2^29, mantissa = round(|v| * 2^(32-4*exp))

operand_kinds.reg: r0..r7; a leading '-' sets the Y negate bit (spec 5.1)
operand_kinds.x_reg: the X field of an ALU op
operand_kinds.y_operand: a register or the instruction's immediate
operand_kinds.reg_x2: a register that also contributes bit 2 to the nibble (unit B)
operand_kinds.transfer: the load/store operands: R and a reference
operand_kinds.label: a jump target
operand_kinds.units: the units a condition word skips

instructions.name: sfu
$doc: D = 8+d, nibble F, bits 7-6 = 00. The function comes from the mode bits 5-4.
Section 6.4 gives cf06 (Y bit 3 = 0) as the reciprocal seed and cf16/cf26/cf36
(Y bit 3 = 1) as the sqrt split / log2 split / ceiling, so the function is
entirely those two bits; Y bit 3 is NOT an independent variant selector there.
The atanh split is the reciprocal-seed form with a logarithm's operand.

instructions.$doc_c: C is the coefficient register, used only when the coefficient mode is 0 (spec 5.2). With an immediate coefficient its bits carry no register, so they are declared free rather than 0.
instructions.$doc_confidence: op2[11:10] (coefficient mode) and coefreg[9] are independent in the *encoding*: the corpus shows every combination occurring. That does not make the *semantics* of each combination known. Each variant therefore carries its own status, and the evidence shows which kind of proof supports it: a formula measured on hardware vs. a pattern seen in code.
instructions.$doc_free: Fields marked {"free": true} are bits the encoding leaves unused for that variant (C, Z, W when a term is absent). They are not required to be zero: no measurement says the hardware ignores them, so the decoder accepts any value and the encoder must preserve whatever it was given.
instructions.$doc_coefreg: bit 9 (spec 5.2) is independent of the coefficient mode: the corpus has both states in every mode, so every combination is declared. Those with bit 9 set are inferred.

banks.$doc: spec 5.5: bits 15-13 of a reference are the bank (from the ARM side)

units.$doc: Body position -> the forms that can describe it, in the order a decoder must try them. A catch-all form (the condition word) comes last.
units.$order: spec 4.2 general order: the ops (A, B, M) and the condition words, then the transfers, then the slot array (N words first, then the references). The assembler sorts a line's units into this order; the disassembler prints them the same way.

directives.$doc: Directives the assembler understands. A directive that changes how one instruction is read goes on its own line before it.

.class.effect: pins the class of the next instruction (spec 4.2 names the class; two classes can share a core layout)

.free.effect: sets bits that the variant leaves free (no defined meaning) in the next instruction; the disassembler writes them back so a round trip preserves what it does not understand
